title: Rights and the rule of law
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 1). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

stops.title: No one is above the law

listen.explanationKey: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
facts: The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the Constitution.
It protects the basic rights of Americans and of people living in the United States.
Freedom of speech and freedom of religion are two of these rights.

newWords.meaning: the first ten amendments to the Constitution
the right to say what you think

readIt.sentence: What is one right in the Bill of Rights?

writeIt.sentence: Freedom of speech is one right.

lessons.title: No one is above the law

listen.explanationKey: What is the rule of law?
facts: The rule of law means everyone must follow the law. Leaders and the government must obey the law too.
No one is above the law.
The government has three branches so one part does not become too powerful. Each branch can check the others. This is called checks and balances.

newWords.meaning: each branch can limit the power of the others
the power of government is split into parts

writeIt.sentence: We elect the President and Congress.

listen.explanationKey: What is the form of government of the United States?
facts: The United States is a republic. The people elect leaders to make laws for them. This is also called a representative democracy.
The economic system of the United States is capitalism, also called a free market economy.
In a free market, people and businesses can own things and decide what to make, buy and sell.

newWords.meaning: a country where the people elect their leaders
an economy where people and businesses own and run things

readIt.sentence: Who can vote in the United States?

writeIt.sentence: Citizens have the right to vote.
